items.question: Write a formal letter (in about 100 words) to the Head of your Department expressing your opinion on the frequent power cuts in the office and their effect on work, and suggesting a practical solution.
items.modelAnswer:
**Model answer**

From: A. Kumar, Assistant Section Officer, Revenue Wing
Date: 20 October 2026

To: The Head of Department, Revenue Wing, District Office

**Subject:** Frequent power cuts affecting office work

Dear Sir,

I wish to bring to your notice the frequent power cuts in our office over the past month, which are seriously affecting our work. Files cannot be processed on time as computers shut down, and public dealing is delayed, drawing complaints from citizens.

In my opinion, an early solution is essential. I respectfully suggest that a backup generator or an inverter be arranged for the main hall, and that the matter be taken up with the electricity department.

I shall be grateful for your kind action.

Yours faithfully,
A. Kumar

**Marking scheme (10 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Correct format (address, date, subject, salutation, close) | 3 |
| Purpose stated clearly + opinion expressed | 2 |
| Relevant details and a practical suggestion | 2 |
| Formal, polite tone | 1 |
| Grammar, spelling, word limit (~100 words) | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** A clear subject line and 'Yours faithfully' are expected in a formal letter. Penalise contractions, missing subject line, or absence of a concrete suggestion.
keyPoints: Use full formal-letter layout: address, date, Subject line, salutation, close, signature.
State the purpose and your opinion in the opening paragraph.
Give relevant details (work delayed, complaints) and one practical suggestion (generator/inverter).
Maintain a polite, formal tone; no contractions.
Format carries 3 marks; keep within ~100 words.
items.source: APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Letter Writing (Item 02); SSC-standard format.

items.question: Write a report (in about 150 words) on a 'Swachh Bharat' cleanliness drive conducted by your office in a nearby village, for the district newsletter.
items.modelAnswer:
**Model answer**

## Office Staff Lead Cleanliness Drive at Peddapuram
*By a Staff Correspondent, Kakinada — 12 October 2026*

As part of the Swachh Bharat Mission, the staff of the District Office organised a cleanliness drive at Peddapuram village on 10 October 2026. About sixty employees, along with local volunteers, took part from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m.

The drive was inaugurated by the District Collector, who stressed that cleanliness is a shared civic duty. Volunteers cleared drains, removed plastic waste from the main road and the school compound, and set up two new dustbins near the market.

A short awareness rally followed, in which children carried placards on waste segregation. The Collector announced that such drives would be held every month. Villagers welcomed the initiative and promised to keep their surroundings clean.

**Marking scheme (15 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Heading + by-line | 2 |
| Opening covers the 5 Ws (what/when/where/who/why) | 4 |
| Factual details in logical order | 4 |
| Third person, past tense, objective tone | 3 |
| Grammar, spelling, word limit (~150 words) | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** Award full marks only for an objective, impersonal account. Penalise first-person narration, present/future tense, or personal opinions.
keyPoints: Open with a heading and a by-line (reporter + place + date).
Cover the 5 Ws in the opening: what, when, where, who, why.
Present factual details in a logical order (inauguration → activity → follow-up).
Write in the third person and past tense with an objective tone.
Keep to ~150 words; format and objectivity carry the most marks.
items.source: APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Report Writing (Item 04); SSC-standard format.

items.question: Write a press release / public appeal (in about 100 words) on behalf of the District Administration asking citizens to conserve water during an expected summer shortage.
items.modelAnswer:
**Model answer**

**PRESS RELEASE / PUBLIC APPEAL — Office of the District Collector, Anantapur**

## Citizens Urged to Conserve Water as Summer Shortage Looms
*Anantapur, 15 March 2026*

With reservoir levels falling and a hot summer forecast, the District Administration appeals to all citizens to use water sparingly in the coming months. Residents are requested to fix leaking taps, avoid washing vehicles with hose-pipes, reuse household water for gardens and store drinking water responsibly.

"Every litre saved today will help our families through the summer," said the District Collector. Tanker services and helpline numbers have been arranged for affected areas. Citizens may contact the control room at the Collectorate for assistance.

**Marking scheme (10 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks |
|---|---|
| Label (Press Release/Appeal) + headline | 2 |
| Dateline (place, date) | 1 |
| Key message first — the appeal and specific actions | 4 |
| A quote / contact detail | 1 |
| Formal tone, grammar, word limit (~100 words) | 2 |

**Examiner notes:** The appeal must name the specific help sought (water-saving actions). Penalise a vague message, a missing dateline, or an informal tone.
keyPoints: Head it with a Press Release/Appeal label and a clear headline.
Add a dateline (place, date) below the headline.
Lead with the key message (inverted pyramid) and list specific water-saving actions.
Include a spokesperson quote and a contact/helpline.
Keep it formal and within ~100 words; naming the specific help sought carries the most marks.
items.source: APPSC 07/2026 English syllabus — Press Release/Appeal (Item 03); SSC-standard format.
